articles.title: Will hordes of influencers, weed smokers and mid-point talkers bring down the US Open?
articles.summary: This year, the noise at the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center has officially become A Problem. But changing it would mean changing society. The first thing you notice while sitting in the upper tiers of Arthur Ashe Stadium is the noise.
body: New York is famously noisy, and the US Open, as the most glamorous annual sporting event in town, has always been loud in sympathy with its environment. Indeed, the brashness of the American grand slam has historically been its major selling point, the signature that distinguishes it from the Australian Open (the “happy slam”), Wimbledon (strawberries and cream, all-white attire, the home of tennis), and the French Open (French). People have been complaining about the volume of the New York crowd for decades. But this year the noise at the US Open feels different. This year noise at the noisy slam has become A Problem.

articles.title: Warning over future of Olympic Games if Brisbane 2032 program is not modernised
articles.summary: Kieren Perkins expresses concern over some traditional sports. Door is open to likes of cricket and netball for Games in Australia. Former gold-medal winning swimmer and Australia’s most senior sport executive, Kieren Perkins, has called on the IOC to modernise the sporting program for Brisbane…
body: The IOC has indicated it wishes to curb a long-term trend of a rise in the number of sports at the Games. Sydney 2000 featured 28 sports, while Los Angeles 2028 is set to feature 36, including many with more than one discipline – for example road and track cycling – that require multiple venues.

Perkins, who is chief executive of government agency the Australian Sports Commission, said he has concerns for the future of the Olympic movement if the Brisbane 2032 program is not updated. “If that program doesn’t look different, then yes, we should start to worry,” he said at the SportNXT conference in Melbourne.

“But if the Olympic movement actually does grasp the challenge that they’ve got, and recognise that while there are some traditional sports that we love dearly, they have no modern relevance whatsoever and there’s others that absolutely have earned and need a more prominent position within the Olympic movement.
“If that’s embraced, then I think we’ll be fine, but if we can’t find a way to navigate through that, then there are question marks about that sustainability.”

articles.title: I can't relate to pressure Eala faces - Gauff
articles.summary: World number four Coco Gauff says she "can't really empathise" with rising Filipino star Alexandra Eala because "she has more pressure than I do".
body: Eala became the first Filipino to win a WTA singles title last month and has risen to 18th in the world rankings.
After losing to Iva Jovic in the third round of the US Open, the 21-year-old got emotional when talking about the huge support she gets from the Philippines.
Gauff will now meet Jovic in the fourth round and the 22-year-old American was asked if she can relate to what Eala, with whom she has played doubles, has to cope with.
"No, I can't at all, because she's the first Filipino player to break a lot of the barriers that she's done, especially on the female side," said Gauff, a two-time Grand Slam winner.

articles.title: Kim Milton Nielsen’s 1998 memories: ‘Hey, you are the man who sent off Beckham’
articles.summary: In an extract from a new book, the Danish former referee recalls sending off the England midfielder for his infamous kick on Diego Simeone. At half-time on 30 June 1998, Kim Milton Nielsen stepped into the changing room at the Geoffroy-Guichard Stadium in Saint-Étienne.
body: Argentina v England. World Cup round of 16. Michael Owen had terrorised Argentina with blistering runs and his breakout goal. A clever free-kick had outsmarted the English defence. Nielsen had awarded two penalties. He couldn’t wait for the second half, but he didn’t know what was coming.

At 37, Nielsen was refereeing his first major international tournament. He’d been trusted with the showcase match. Tensions between Argentina and England had simmered since the 1982 Falklands war, and deepened through controversial World Cup ​clashes – Geoff Hurst’s goal in 1966; Diego Maradona’s handball 20 years later. A loss for either side would be colossal.

Diego Simeone clattered into David Beckham. Nielsen blew his whistle to book Simeone. Simeone leaned on Beckham and tugged his hair. Beckham flicked his boot; Simeone fell. Nielsen blew again. Red card for Beckham.

But it wasn’t going to be that easy. Sending off Beckham, a global superstar, at a World Cup with a full half still to play. A voice in Nielsen’s head whispered: was it really violent? Didn’t Simeone provoke it? Then he recognised the voice. He’d heard it before. It had nearly beaten him. He knew what to do.

articles.title: Wallabies’ Carter Gordon set for stint on sidelines after breaking leg in latest injury blow
articles.summary: Flyhalf sustains injury in weekend’s draw with Argentina. Expected to miss Springboks Test and Bledisloe Cup series. The Wallabies are bracing to be without first-choice playmaker Carter Gordon for the Bledisloe Cup and a clash with world champions South Africa in the latest injury blow for the…
body: Gordon fell to the ground in agony after attacking the line late in the weekend’s 28-28 draw with Argentina in Mendoza.
The side doesn’t land back in Australia until Monday night but it is understood scans post-game revealed the 25-year-old had suffered a leg fracture that will keep him sidelined for two months.

That injury would rule him out of the Wallabies’ Perth Test against the Springboks on 26 September, as well as next month’s two-Test Bledisloe Cup series. There is hope he would be fit in time to face England at Twickenham on 8 November.
It’s the latest injury blow for the luckless playmaker, who suffered a serious back injury that derailed his NRL cameo and has battled various leg niggles since returning to rugby barely a year ago.

articles.summary: Hibernian head coach David Gray is under increasing pressure after a drab defeat at St Johnstone on Sunday, but what has gone wrong in recent weeks?
body: Ten days ago, Hibernian were six minutes away from creating history and reaching the league phase of the Conference League.
David Gray, already lauded in Leith for his Scottish Cup heroics as a player, would have been glorified to an even greater extent.
Never before has a Hibs side reached league phase - or group stage - football in Europe. They could almost touch it, and the riches that come with it.
But then there was a complete capitulation against Gent as they fell at the final hurdle for the second year running.

articles.title: Marnus Labuschagne survives cut as Australia name Test squad to face South Africa
articles.summary: Top-order batsman Marnus Labuschagne was named in the Australia squad for next month's three-Test tour of South Africa on Monday despite a run of poor recent form that has called into question his international future.
body: The right-hander, who was born in South Africa, was dropped from the one-day squad for a tour of southern Africa last week but retained in the 16-strong party which will play tests in Durban, Gqeberha and Cape Town in October.

All-rounder Cooper Connolly, paceman Michael Neser and left-arm spinner Matthew Kuhnemann are the additions to the squad that lost a first Test on home soil to Bangladesh last month before rallying to level the series.

Labuschagne's 36 runs over three innings in the Bangladesh series had many questioning the seven-year grip he has held on the number three spot in the batting order, although he does have ⁠a decent record in South Africa.

Chief selector George Bailey said: “Not shying away from the fact that we'd like some more runs from Marn, that's clear. But we're also confident that he can still make a positive contribution to that squad.

articles.title: England's push for 'world-class' all-rounders to close gap on Australia
articles.summary: England Women's national selector Lydia Greenway laid out her plan for the side to close the gap on the world's best, Australia, with a push for 'world-class' allrounders at the heart of their strategy.
body: As part of that plan, all-rounders Dani Gibson and Freya Kemp have been starters throughout the summer, which included T20 series wins over New Zealand and India, as well as a run to the final of the T20 World Cup on home soil - before being beaten by Australia.
Charlotte Edwards' side were also well beaten by India in a historic first women's Test at Lord's, but they ended their summer on a high with a 3-0 ODI series sweep of Ireland.
"We don't want to be behind Australia all the time, we've got to close that gap," Greenway told Sky Sports Cricket during the third ODI win over Ireland on Sunday.
"And when you look at Australia, and how they're lined up in their top seven, they've probably got three or four bowling options - so we need to look at how we can do that.

articles.title: Toto Wolff uneasy as Mercedes drivers fought at Monza: “That could have ended in disaster”
articles.summary: Toto Wolff believes the battle for victory between Kimi Antonelli and George Russell at the Italian Grand Prix “could have ended in disaster” – and the Mercedes Formula 1 squad “would have looked like idiots”.
body: Antonelli started his home race down in 19th, courtesy of a grid penalty for exceeding his power unit allowance, but fought his way up to second place in just 16 laps.

A 12-lap battle with Russell ensued, with the Silver Arrows trading the race lead several times, until a virtual safety car intervention provided the opportunity of a pitstop for Antonelli, who emerged back on track just 14 seconds behind his team-mate.

Fresh tyres meant the 20-year-old Italian caught the lead car with six laps remaining, and the decisive battle for victory occurred then – with a scare on lap 49, as Russell cut Turn 2 while Antonelli slid wide into the gravel trap.

They still achieved a 1-2, with Antonelli leading Russell by four seconds and Max Verstappen by 15s under the chequered flag. However, it definitely wasn’t comfortable for Mercedes team principal Wolff, who considered reaching out to his drivers’ race engineers, Marcus Dudley and Peter ‘Bono’ Bonnington.

articles.title: The NFL is back! The race to Super Bowl 61 starts here
articles.summary: 285 games. Eight countries. Four continents. Six time zones. 22 weeks. 32 teams. One champion. And five gold rings - oops, sorry Jayden Daniels. The 2026 NFL season is here.
body: Seven months ago, discarded embers of confetti would pave the way for our meandering walk towards the exit at an emptying Levi's Stadium as the curtain closed on Super Bowl 60, footballing disciples reluctant to accept it was all over for another year as they braced for annual hibernation.

Sam Darnold had just crowned one of sport's great fairy-tale redemption stories, Aden Durde had just made British sporting history, Mike Macdonald's Dark Side defense had just tormented Drake Maye and Bad Bunny had just delivered a clinic in reggaeton rage-bait in the face of orange-tinged white-housed backlash over his landmark half-time show.

Seattle Seahawks players and coaches alike rejoiced over childhood dreams fulfilled in the company of loved ones, while for others the clock had already reset, for football rarely dwells too long on the present.
The countdown is finally over. From here on, there shall be no more football-less Sundays until February. The road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles starts here.

articles.title: Huge week ahead! How to watch the Solheim Cup live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Team Europe aim to reclaim the Solheim Cup on home soil when they host Team USA in the Netherlands this week, exclusively live in the UK and Ireland on Sky Sports.
body: Three-time major champion Anna Nordqvist captains a strong European team at Bernardus Golf, with England's Charley Hull making her eighth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance and Lottie Woad among the rookies in action.

The hosts are looking to earn their first outright victory since their famous 15-13 away success in 2021, having scrambled a dramatic 14-14 tie to retain in Spain in 2023 before Team USA secured a 15.5-12.5 victory the following year.

World No 1 Nelly Korda headlines Team USA and is a two-time major winner this season, with captain Angela Stanford now looking to lead the visitors to their first away success in the biennial contest since 2015.

A tight contest is expected in front of a strong Dutch crowd, where both teams are confident of securing the trophy, while Sky Sports will offer round-the-clock coverage from one of the biggest events in the golfing calendar.
